title: Introduce Elm RAG playground with stepper UI and lightweight telemetry
author: Anika Patel
release_notes: Add a new browser-friendly Elm RAG playground example demonstrating incremental tool-calls, stepper-guided prompt construction, and optional telemetry hooks for Console integration.
description:
Motivation: we want a compact, dependency-light example that shows how to wire a retrieval-augmented generation flow into a client-side playground with explicit stepper guidance and observable telemetry. The Elm playground is intentionally small: it runs in the browser, delegates model calls to Redwood's hosted API via a thin proxy, and includes an optional telemetry adaptor that emits structured events to Console-compatible endpoints.

What this PR does: Adds an Elm-based quickstart example and docs page. Core features: a guided stepper UI that walks users through query -> retrieval selection -> prompt authoring -> tool invocation -> answer formatting; a series of canned retrieval backends (in-memory docs, GitHub gist loader); a lightweight telemetry hook that emits small JSON events for token/cost estimation and step timings; minimal CI to build and smoke test the Elm bundle.

Checklist:
- [x] Add Elm playground scaffold and stepper UI
- [x] Add telemetry adaptor and example Console mapping
- [x] Add docs page to docs site quickstarts with screenshots and code snippets
- [x] Add CI workflow for building and linting the example
- [x] Add a small README and license notes for third-party deps

Why Elm? The example targets users who want a strongly-typed, tiny front-end demo that can be embedded in docs or run locally with zero Node server besides the proxy. Elm enforces a single-update loop which makes demonstrating the stepper transitions and retry/fallback behavior easier to reason about in examples.

Security note: the example proxies API keys through a dev-only server included as a tiny Express shim (examples/elm-playground/proxy). README makes it explicit this is for local development only; production deployments must use server-side key management.

Links and related work: Inspired by earlier WASM/edge quickstarts and the RAG tool-calling workshops; this complements redwood-examples/wasm and redwood-quickstarts by focusing on a minimal client-side UX pattern and telemetry bindings. Related Linear: ENG-3152. Support ticket SUP-731 requested a low-ceremony browser demo for developer outreach.

- "feat: add stepper UI and retrieval adapters" -- stepper implementation, in-memory corpus, gist loader
- "feat: telemetry: emit step events + Console adaptor" -- telemetry adaptor, config, sample mapping
- "docs: add quickstart guide and screenshots" -- docs page wired into site, images and copy
- "ci: add elm example build workflow and smoke test" -- CI YAML and basic smoke checks

High-level changed files: 
- "examples/elm-playground/src/Main.elm" -- main app + stepper glue
- "examples/elm-playground/src/Telemetry.elm" -- telemetry adaptor and event formatter
- "examples/elm-playground/README.md" -- how-to, dev proxy, security guidance
- "docs/site/content/quickstarts/elm-client-rag-playground.md" -- docs site quickstart page
- "ci/workflows/elm-example.yml" -- GitHub Actions workflow to build and smoke test the example
- "examples/elm-playground/proxy/server.js" -- tiny dev proxy shim (dev use only)

Notes on scope: The example intentionally avoids shipping a full model client in Elm; network calls go to the proxy that forwards to Redwood hosted API or a user-provided endpoint. This keeps the example focused on UX and observability patterns rather than browser-level auth models.

review_comments: Diego Morales: Nice small example; can we make the telemetry payload opt-in by default? People will run this locally and we shouldn't emit events without explicit consent.
Anika Patel: Agree, telemetry is behind a \"optInTelemetry\" flag in the UI and off by default. README emphasizes that the Console mapping is optional and requires manual configuration.

Claire Zhang: The stepper looks good, but we should add a 'replay' button so users can step backwards through previous query states for debugging. Also suggest a small e2e smoke test that runs the stepper headlessly.
Anika Patel: Added replay support and a smoke check in the CI job (runs elm-test with a headless stepper scenario).
Priya Shah: Docs copy should call out that the proxy is dev-only and link to Private deployment guidance for production key handling.
Anika Patel: Updated docs to include explicit production guidance and a short checklist for migrating off the dev proxy.
ci_summary: Initial run: fail (linting due to unused import), fix pushed; subsequent runs: pass (build+test+linter). Workflow: elm-example.yml runs 'elm make', 'elm-test', and a small smoke URL healthcheck against the dev proxy container.
notes_for_backport: None. Example-level change; no runtime/library surface area impacted.
